supporting_observations.claim: The repeated HTTPS checks are attributable to C:\Program Files\ChartMate\cmupdate.exe, which started at 13:37:41 and made connections through the proxy to update.chartmate-imaging.com at 13:37:44, 13:42:50, 13:48:02, 13:52:36, 13:57:55, 14:02:39, and 14:07:42. This matches the inventory description of the approved ChartMate updater checking about every five minutes.
The observed ChartMate connections use the configured explicit proxy at 10.30.20.30:8080; the endpoint-side records identify cmupdate.exe as the initiating process for those connections.

A UserAssist registry record contains an encoded path that decodes to C:\Windows\System32\mstsc.exe, but the supplied records do not establish a process start, destination, or successful remote session. This is a separate item to verify because the inventory says remote administration is done only from WS-OHADDAD-01.

Explorer changed the user's Hidden and ShowSuperHidden settings, and Explorer loaded 7-zip.dll with signature status unavailable. These events are observed but do not, by themselves, establish malicious activity or a connection to the periodic HTTPS checks.

known_telemetry_limitations: The ChartMate proxy records show CONNECT requests and tunnel byte counts, not the encrypted HTTPS contents or the precise update data transferred.
The supplied records do not show a process-creation event for mstsc.exe or identify any remote-access destination or session outcome.
The evidence is limited to the supplied records and does not establish that all endpoint, proxy, firewall, or remote-access telemetry for the review window is present.
claims_not_established: That the ChartMate updater downloaded or executed a specific update payload.
That mstsc.exe was successfully launched or used to connect to another host.
That the registry changes or 7-zip.dll load were malicious or related to the ChartMate connections.
That no other relevant activity occurred outside the supplied records.
additional_evidence_needed: Check endpoint process-creation and EDR telemetry around 14:10 UTC to confirm whether mstsc.exe ran and, if so, its parent, user, command line, and target.
Check firewall, network, and remote-access logs for connections from WS-BCARTER-01 to RDP or other remote-administration services during the review window.
If update integrity is in question, obtain the ChartMate updater's file/signature details and update or download logs.
